summary: Streaming chat disconnects or stalls mid-generation (SSE/WebSocket) for customer-facing chat sessions
description: Issue summary: Multiple customers reported streaming chat sessions disconnecting or stalling mid-generation over SSE/WebSocket during peak load windows. Impact: Customer-facing chat flows drop mid-response, causing incomplete assistant responses and degraded UX for VeloxHealth (enterprise). Environment: prod-us-east, primarily affecting sessions routed to redwood-3b-v1 and fallback redwood-7b-q4_0. Observed during 2026-02-28 09:40 - 11:20 UTC. Severity chosen due to enterprise SLA and session data loss.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Open a streaming chat session (SSE or WebSocket) with api.redwood.ai on prod-us-east using an enterprise API key.
2) Send a prompt that triggers multi-turn generation (response length > 800 tokens) or includes streaming-enabled settings (stream=true, max_tokens=2000).
3) Observe the stream: connection either disconnects (client sees close) or stalls with no new tokens for >20s while backend indicates generating state.
4) Confirm with curl/WS tool that connection closed with HTTP 499/504 or TCP RST from proxy in some cases.
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support (Alex) determined multiple customers and sessions impacted; high correlation with increased queued requests in dedicated pools and a recent infra deployment to proxy/idle-timeout config.
SRE (Diego) examined serving-runtime traces and observed requests in 'generating' state while proxy showed client-close (499) and occasional 504s for long-running streaming connections.

Hypothesis 1: Regression in proxy idle/keepalive alignment causing upstream to close streaming sockets when token generation stalls for >15s. Evidence: gateway websocket_ping_timeout log entries and recent PR that adjusted proxy keepalive from 45s -> 20s (github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1423).

Hypothesis 2: Serving runtime introduced a KV cache lock contention under bursty long-context workloads leading to stalls between token flushes. Evidence: runtime logs showing 'waiting_for_kvcache_lock' and increased tail latency for token flushes around 2026-02-28 09:40 UTC.
Reproduction attempts: Engineering reproduced at lower QPS by replaying customer prompts; observed intermittent stalls when using redwood-3b-v1 with long contexts and concurrent cache writes.
Correlated issues: SUP-8421 and SUP-43210 show similar symptom patterns; internal investigation ticket INT-330 tracks the runtime cache lock fixes.
Short-term mitigation: Reverted proxy keepalive change in staging and applied a configuration patch to prod to increase streaming idle thresholds to 60s while we investigate runtime contensions.

resolution: Hotfix: Reverted proxy keepalive reduction and increased streaming idle timeout to 60s in prod; deployed runtime backpressure mitigation to reduce KV cache contention for long-context streaming requests. Full fix: runtime patch to KV cache lock (PR github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/987) rolled out to canary then prod. Follow-up actions: create a streaming disconnect runbook, add end-to-end regression tests for streaming under long-context/high-concurrency, and track capacity guidance for dedicated pools. Customer compensated with 10% credit for the impacted billing period.
